note: Occupationally he fits: an accountant with his own office and a wife in the same profession, established enough that his hours have shrunk from 2am finishes to 9pm over the years. Health is plainly the neglected area rather than a crisis — two years without structured training while everything else got attention — and he is not deconditioned or gym-averse, at 185 lb and 5'10", playing soccer daily with his kids and already building a basement gym. Income is the clear miss: 'we're full of bills', multiple mortgages, two children, a self-declared ceiling of $1,000 a month and a purchase that needs joint sign-off from an equally cost-conscious spouse. Good-to-great is the closer call and I score it a miss — his own framing is comeback rather than optimisation ('I've been out of shape for a while', 'I let it go too much', 'this is kind of my last jump into it'), and the trigger was watching a younger wife get ahead of him rather than wanting to convert good into great. He pushes back on being seen as far gone ('I don't think I'm 240 pounds'), which is why this is edge and not outside. Same pattern as the Francisco Vega assessment already in the ICP file: fits the profile, needs instalments, closer to rescue than to good-to-great.
